characterization_methods.key_findings: Peak broadening and a change of strongest reflection from (111) in the solutionized state to (220) from MAF-1; for MAF-3: avg. crystallite size 10.87 nm, avg. microstrain 6.13 × 10^-3, dislocation density 7.5 × 10^15 m^-2.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Scan speed 2° per minute, step size 0.02°, 2θ range 40°-120°; electropolished samples; instrumental broadening from standard silicon subtracted
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine dislocation density, average crystallite size, lattice microstrain and texture (via Williamson-Hall analysis)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EBSD with equivalent grain size method; grain boundaries defined by misorientation >15°
characterization_methods.key_findings: MAF-3: high-angle boundary fraction 0.24, low-angle boundary fraction 0.759 (~0.75, maximum of the series); grain size reduced to 20 μm; texture progressively randomized.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Electropolished samples; image quality maps with high-angle (15°-180°) and low-angle (1°-15°) boundaries; 60 μm scale bars
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine average grain size, grain boundary fractions and texture (inverse pole figure maps of the normal/pressing direction)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EBSD KAM maps (unique color map, 60 μm scale bar)
characterization_methods.key_findings: MAF-3 shows an average KAM value of 0.87°, indicating a higher level of plastic deformation (uniformity attributed to tri-axial deformation).
characterization_methods.purpose: Quantify local misorientation / stored deformation strain

characterization_methods.key_findings: MAF-3: yield strength 1279 MPa (text)/1289 MPa (Table 2), UTS 1415 MPa, total elongation 13.7%, uniform elongation 3%, work hardening 126 MPa.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature, strain rate 1 × 10^-3 s^-1; miniature round specimens (gauge length 16 mm, Ø4 mm gauge) cut from the located area of the MAF sample
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the effect of multiaxial forging on tensile strength after each MAF pass

analytical_models.equation_role: Predict flow stress incorporating dislocation-density and grain-size strengthening into the classical J-C framework
analytical_models.model_note: Encoded in the VUMAT subroutine using six state-dependent variables: SDV1 equivalent plastic strain, SDV2 equivalent plastic strain rate, SDV3 dislocation density ρ_f, SDV4 flow stress, SDV5 yield strength, SDV6 grain size d_f (Table 3).
Non-linear fit of experimental dislocation density vs imposed strain; R-Square (COD) = 0.98554.
Exponential fit of grain size vs equivalent strain; R-Square (COD) = 0.99052.
Eq. 4 relates yield-strength gain from grain refinement over the grain-size range 50–13 μm.
α = 0.24, M = 3.0, G = 61 GPa; for FCC austenite b = a/√2.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Workpiece modelled as deformable body with dimensions 30 mm × 20 mm × 20 mm; mesh sensitivity analysis gave a mesh size of 0.6 mm with 41382 hexahedral (C3D8R, reduced integration with hourglass control) elements; die and punch treated as discrete rigid bodies; punch given a controlled displacement of 10 mm in the Y (height) direction while the die is fixed; material flow permitted only in X (flow direction), constrained in Z (constrained direction); workpiece-rigid body contact friction coefficient 0.15; steady-state MAF simulated by mapping deformation fields from previous passes to the current one.
computational_details.simulation_method: 3-D finite element simulation of the MAF process using a modified Johnson-Cook constitutive model (elastic-plastic return-mapping in a user material subroutine)
computational_details.software_used: ABAQUS/Explicit with a VUMAT user subroutine
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Predicted dislocation density and grain size at the location in Fig. 3(a) compared with measured results (XRD for dislocation density, EBSD for grain size); the modified J-C model with FEA shows good agreement for MAF-1, MAF-3 and MAF-5. Yield strength prediction (Fig. 13) tracks the experimental strengthening closely around 3 passes but deviates (underestimates) at 1 and 5 passes.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: Low-angle grain boundary (subgrain) formation and subdivision
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: After 3 MAF passes the low-angle boundary (1°-15°) fraction reaches its maximum value of ~0.75 (0.759 per EBSD legend) while the high-angle boundary (15°-180°) fraction drops to 0.24, reflecting extensive grain subdivision by low-angle boundaries.

interfaces.interface_notes: The paper reports grain-boundary misorientation statistics rather than discrete phase interfaces; the κ-carbide reflections remain unchanged before and after MAF (Fig. 5).
interfaces.phase_evolution: No deformation twinning occurs in this alloy during MAF; the austenite is stable (no martensite formed). Annealing twin boundary fraction is very small. Texture is progressively randomized as the number of passes increases.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Relative to solution-annealed MAF-0, the MAF-3 yield-strength increase decomposes into 669 MPa from the dislocation-density difference and 240 MPa from grain refinement (Table 2).

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cast ingot of Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8 C low-density steel homogenized at 1200 °C for 2 h (material preparation common to all MAF states).
Hot forged between 1200 °C and 900 °C ensuring more than 60% deformation with intermediate heating, then water quenched.
Forged material solutionized at 1050 °C for 1 h and water quenched to retain maximum austenite phase; this is the MAF-0 (0 pass) baseline state from which every MAF pass starts.
Sample and die heated to 250 °C and soaked for two hours prior to MAF (warm deformation condition, chosen below the recrystallization temperature).

MAF carried out along three orthogonal directions on a 100-ton hydraulic press; ram moved at a steady speed of 1 mm/s; billet (30 × 20 × 20 mm) lubricated with MoS2 before pressing; 3 passes performed, defining the MAF-3 state.
processing_steps.reduction_ratio: 33% normal strain per pass; cumulative equivalent strain 1.4 after 3 passes

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tested on an INSTRON hydraulic universal testing machine; two round tensile samples per pass to confirm reliability; elastic length subtracted from elongation to give plastic strain.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: Miniature round tensile specimen: gauge length 16 mm, overall length 26.5 mm, fillet radius R1, gauge diameter Ø4 mm, shoulder Ø7.2 mm (Fig. 3(b))

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curves in Fig. 10; MAF-3 (blue) curve peaks near 1400 MPa at small strain and drops to about 1240 MPa at strain ≈0.13, failing early (strength-ductility trade-off).

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Distribution becomes narrower/more uniform with increasing passes; fragmented, multi-colour banded structure at MAF-3 (Fig. 7(g)).
grain_structure.texture: Texture randomized relative to the strongly textured MAF-0; IPF shows many different directions parallel to the pressing direction.

phases_present.texture: progressively randomized with increasing passes (weak texture)

microstructure_list.region: Analysed central plate along the pressing direction (location shown in Fig. 3(a))

phases_present.texture: change of strongest reflection from γ(111) in the solutionized state to γ(220) from MAF-1 onward, indicating texturing

microstructure_list.region: Analysed area for XRD (central plate, pressing direction)

structures.overall_structure: Austenite-based (FCC) Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8 C low-density steel; XRD shows a dominantly single austenite (γ) phase with retained κ-carbide reflections. After 3 MAF passes the grains are refined and heavily subdivided by a dense low-angle boundary network (low-angle boundary fraction at its maximum) with a progressively randomized texture.

unmapped_findings: MAF-3 equivalent plastic strain imparted = 1.4 (third MAF pass).

Dislocation density for MAF-3 is reported inconsistently: Table 1 gives 7.5 × 10^15 m^-2, whereas the Mechanical properties text states 7.8 × 10^15 m^-2 (about ten times that of the solutionized material).
Yield strength for MAF-3 is reported inconsistently: the Mechanical properties text gives 1279 MPa, while Table 2 lists measured YS = 1289 MPa for 3 Pass.
MAF-3 average grain size by EBSD = 20 μm (reduced from 50 μm at MAF-0 and 35 μm at MAF-1).
MAF-3 high-angle grain boundary fraction = 0.24; low-angle grain boundary fraction = ~0.75 (0.759), the maximum of the MAF series.
MAF-3 amount of work hardening = 126 MPa; UTS (1415 MPa) and YS diverge less than in earlier passes.
In this alloy there is no deformation twinning during MAF; the annealing twin boundary fraction is negligible (0.007 in MAF-1 and 0.003 in MAF-5).

FE simulation: after 3 passes the predicted yield strength agrees closely with the measured value (curves nearly converge between 1 and 3 passes); simulation underestimates YS most strongly at 5 passes.

FE simulation of specimen shape does not accurately replicate the experimental distortion, attributed to the absence of crystallographic texture effects in the simulation; the simulated strength is lower than the experimental value.
Simulated yield strength depends on depth from the surface of the forged sample: maximum at the centre and decreasing towards the surface (Fig. 14, SDV5 range ≈ +6.994e+02 to +1.358e+03).
